# Switchbak

> Switchbak carries the sessions of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) from a Mac to the warehouse of an organization. Each pull request then gets a Receipt: a check run and a comment that record the sessions behind the change.

- The client runs only on a Mac with Apple silicon. It does not run on an Intel Mac, on Windows or on Linux.
- Install with `brew install switchbackai/tap/switchbak`, then run `switchbak login` and sign in with GitHub or Google (`switchbak login --device` on a machine with no browser). A GitHub login makes the account and its workspace; a Google login needs a workspace made first at https://app.switchbak.dev/signup. The uploads start when login ends. The Account page of app.switchbak.dev links GitHub and Google to one account. It needs no GitHub App.
- `switchbak connect` installs the GitHub App, so that pull requests get a Receipt.
- `switchbak status` prints the state of an installation. Its first line is `ready     installed ✓  authenticated ✓  connected ✓`; before the first session it ends `connected, waiting for first session — run an agent`, which is not a failure. Without the GitHub App it prints `github    Receipts on pull requests are off`; uploads and Audits still run. `switchbak audit -json <path>` prints the Audit of a session as JSON.
- Each member of an organization can read every session of it. A GitHub member is a person with access to an installation of the GitHub App that the organization connected. When the access ends, run `switchbak login` after access returns. `switchbak logout` logs the Mac out and removes the keychain items; it keeps the config and the launch agents. An admin removes a member on the members page.
